_about: The one path every local (Ollama) model call takes: local_llm.py. Found 10 Nov 2026 in Ollama's server.log: one tutor call sent an 8555-token prompt, which the server cut to 4098 tokens, system prompt included. With no num_predict and no client timeout the model then generated ~78,000 tokens over 20 minutes; a later call ran for 1h3m. Ollama has one slot per model, so every other caller queued behind it, and a caller with a different num_ctx left the model 'Stopping...' until that finished: the wedge. So here, for every real call: the GPU lease, ONE num_ctx per model, a cap on generated tokens, a timeout, and a check for a wedged server.
_host: Base URL when host_env is unset. A bare host:port in the env gets http:// put in front.
_num_ctx: ONE context per model: a call's own num_ctx is ignored, because a model asked for a different num_ctx is unloaded and reloaded, and a reload queued behind a running request is what sticks in 'Stopping'. A model not named in num_ctx_by_model gets the brain's context (context: env wins, then file's key path: AGENTS.md, 8192, measured). A job that needs less context trims its prompt. Embedding calls are left alone: their model has its own single context.
_num_predict: Most tokens one reply may generate. A call that names none gets num_predict; one that asks for more is capped at num_predict_max. Without a cap, a model whose prompt was cut short can generate until the call is killed (10 Nov: 78k tokens).
_chars_per_token: Rough chars per token for warning about a prompt too long for num_ctx less num_predict. Measured 10 Nov: a tutor chunk of lecture text came to about 2.6 chars per token; 2.5 errs on the long side. A prompt over the limit is logged, not refused: Ollama would cut it from the front.
_timeout_s: Every real call has a client timeout: by job, else by kind (chat, generate, embed), else timeout_s. A call that names its own timeout keeps the shorter of the two.
_lease: Every real call holds .review/gpu.lease in the main checkout (orchestra/local_team/lease.py), waiting up to wait_s for it. Re-entrant: a lease this process holds, or one the parent process holds and names in owner_env (orchestra/consult.py sets it for the tutor it runs), counts as held. Still busy after the wait: on_busy raise = the call fails with LeaseBusy (a TimeoutError, so callers' error handling classes it as the server's fault), run = the call goes ahead anyway with a log line. Denisse's own replies (denisse_brain) wait a short while and then run, so a long eval never leaves Chuen without an answer; the autopilot (atrium_autopilot) waits briefly and then uses its fallback rule rather than stall the runner. A streamed call (stream=True) is not supported: the lease would end before the stream. Calls in one process are also serialised by a lock. The lease ttl is the call's timeout plus ttl_margin_s.
_wedge: Before each real call, and after one that timed out or lost its connection, /api/ps is read (ps_timeout_s). Wedged = a model whose expiry passed more than stopping_s ago (what `ollama ps` shows as 'Stopping...'), or /api/ps itself timing out. A refused connection (Ollama not running) is not a wedge: nothing is started that Chuen quit. With auto_restart, a wedged server is restarted: the kill commands for this platform, then start (detached, env vars expanded), then up to up_wait_s for it to answer. At most once per min_restart_interval_s (state file). Every check that finds a wedge, and every restart, is a line in log (main checkout). No restart commands for a platform = log only.
